items.title: Navalia: Advancing Cowork Agents through Verifiable Task Synthesis and Long-Horizon Post-Training
items.summary: Navalia is a framework designed to advance Cowork Agents by combining verifiable task synthesis and long-horizon post-training. It uses corporate financial reports to semantically select evidence and construct executable computation chains for generating analytical tasks with traceable dependencies. Independent LLM review and programmatic checks are employed to verify evidence consistency and answer correctness. These verified tasks are then used for trajectory collection, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning to enhance long-horizon execution. Navalia consistently improves evidence integration, tool use, and long-horizon task execution across various benchmarks.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Navalia: Advancing Cowork Agents through Verifiable Task Synthesis and Long-Horizon Post-Training" details a framework designed to advance Cowork Agents through verifiable task synthesis and long-horizon post-training. The framework utilizes corporate financial reports to semantically select evidence and construct executable computation chains for generating analytical tasks with traceable dependencies. Independent large language model review and programmatic checks are then employed to verify evidence consistency and answer correctness. These verified tasks facilitate trajectory collection, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning to enhance long-horizon execution. Navalia demonstrates consistent improvement in evidence integration, tool use, and long-horizon task execution across various benchmarks. This development indicates a pathway for creating more reliable and capable AI agents capable of complex, multi-step analytical work.

items.title: Industrial Agentic AI: LLM-Driven New-Generation Agents for Smart Manufacturing
items.summary: Large language models enable agents to plan and execute tasks, presenting opportunities for smart manufacturing. Challenges in dynamic environments and physical constraints limit the direct use of general-purpose agents in this sector. The paper systematically analyzes industrial agents, establishing a taxonomy for scenarios, embodiment, and capabilities. It proposes a four-layer system architecture for closed-loop task execution of these agents. The work provides a structured reference for designing, developing, and applying industrial agents across the manufacturing lifecycle.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Industrial Agentic AI: LLM-Driven New-Generation Agents for Smart Manufacturing" presents an analysis of large language models enabling agents to plan and execute tasks for smart manufacturing, establishing a taxonomy for scenarios, embodiment, and capabilities of industrial agents. The research systematically analyzes industrial agents and proposes a four-layer system architecture designed for closed-loop task execution of these agents. This framework provides a structured reference for designing, developing, and applying industrial agents throughout the manufacturing lifecycle, addressing the challenges posed by dynamic environments and physical constraints. The work details the methodology for establishing this taxonomy and the proposed architectural system. This research indicates a pathway for integrating advanced language model capabilities into physical industrial systems for enhanced automation. Future developments will focus on the practical deployment and refinement of these agentic systems in complex manufacturing settings.

items.title: MAMath-Bench: Process-Aware and Robust Evaluation of Multimodal Multi-Agent Mathematical Reasoning
items.summary: MAMath-Bench is a process-aware benchmark designed to evaluate the multimodal mathematical reasoning of multi-agent systems. It consists of 1,003 problems across 11 mathematical categories, involving text, images, and audio modalities. The benchmark assesses systems based on problem-solving correctness, reasoning-process reliability, and robustness to adversarial perturbations. Evaluations show that multi-agent collaboration does not always improve final accuracy but can enhance reasoning coverage. Furthermore, current systems remain susceptible to errors introduced by adversarial reasoning-chain perturbations.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "MAMath-Bench: Process-Aware and Robust Evaluation of Multimodal Multi-Agent Mathematical Reasoning" details a benchmark designed to evaluate the multimodal mathematical reasoning of multi-agent systems. The benchmark consists of one thousand three problems across eleven mathematical categories involving text, images, and audio modalities, assessing systems based on problem-solving correctness, reasoning-process reliability, and robustness to adversarial perturbations. Evaluations indicate that multi-agent collaboration does not consistently improve final accuracy but can increase reasoning coverage. Current systems demonstrate susceptibility to errors introduced by adversarial reasoning-chain perturbations. This research provides a structured method for assessing complex multimodal reasoning in artificial intelligence systems. Further research will focus on mitigating adversarial vulnerabilities in multi-agent mathematical problem-solving.

items.title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring
items.summary: MedPAO-Assist is an edge-deployable, modality-aware agentic AI framework designed for structuring radiology reports. It generates structured reports directly from radiologist dictation and voice commands, minimizing reliance on cloud services. The system is capable of handling four imaging modalities, including Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, and Brain MRI. It utilizes a Small Language Model and an Extract-Ground-Generate paradigm for concept extraction and structured report generation. This agentic system supports a "no-touch" workflow requiring no external connectivity or keyboard input.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring" reports on a framework designed for structuring radiology reports using agentic artificial intelligence. The system is capable of handling four imaging modalities including Chest X-ray Chest CT Abdomen CT and Brain MRI. It employs a Small Language Model and an Extract-Ground-Generate paradigm for concept extraction and structured report generation. This agentic system facilitates a no-touch workflow requiring no external connectivity or keyboard input. This development indicates a shift toward deploying complex AI capabilities directly onto edge devices for specialized medical applications. Further research is anticipated in expanding modality support and deployment scalability.

items.title: DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution
items.summary: DataPraxis is a framework that scales analytics tasks by evolving workspaces with verified findings and artifacts. It progressively enriches workspaces and inherits these results to uncover deeper analytical questions. The framework constructs tasks from accumulated findings and their dependencies, verifying analytical results during evolution and assembly. A dataset called DataPraxis-5K was created from these verified trajectories to train larger models like DataPraxis-27B and DataPraxis-35B-A3B. These models achieved competitive performance on benchmarks, surpassing frontier models.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution" details a framework designed to scale analytics tasks by evolving workspaces with verified findings and artifacts. The framework progressively enriches workspaces and inherits these results to uncover deeper analytical questions by constructing tasks from accumulated findings and their dependencies while verifying analytical results during evolution and assembly. A specific dataset named DataPraxis-5K was generated from these verified trajectories to train larger models such as DataPraxis-27B and DataPraxis-35B-A3B, which demonstrated competitive performance on benchmarks surpassing frontier models. This methodology establishes a method for systematically scaling complex analytical problem-solving through verifiable workspace evolution. Future developments in verifiable data-driven model training are expected to focus on similar iterative refinement processes.

items.title: STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites
items.summary: A Set Transformer model is presented to estimate X-ray transmission in polymer composites, bypassing computationally expensive Monte Carlo simulations. The model maps molecular constituents, their mass fractions, and physical descriptors directly to the transmission ratio in milliseconds. It utilizes chemistry-pretrained transformer embeddings from ChemBERTa for each constituent. Training data is generated via a PENELOPE/penEasy pipeline using simulated radiation data across various tube voltages. The method achieves a low mean squared error of $(1.12 \pm 0.56)\times10^{-4}$ with high accuracy and significantly faster inference times.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites" reports on a Set Transformer model developed to estimate X-ray transmission in polymer composites. The model achieves a low mean squared error of 1.12 times ten to the minus four with high accuracy and significantly faster inference times. The methodology involves mapping molecular constituents, their mass fractions, and physical descriptors directly to the transmission ratio in milliseconds. The system utilizes chemistry-pretrained transformer embeddings from ChemBERTa for each constituent, and training data was generated through a PENELOPE/penEasy pipeline using simulated radiation data across various tube voltages. This approach bypasses computationally expensive Monte Carlo simulations by directly relating molecular information to the transmission ratio. This advancement demonstrates the capability of machine learning to accelerate material property prediction in complex composites.

items.title: To Keep or Not to Keep: Learning KV Cache Retention in Disaggregated LLM Serving Systems
items.summary: Disaggregated LLM serving separates prefill and decode, complicating cache retention decisions by adding network transfer costs. KVLearn is a learning-based framework designed for cost-aware KV-cache retention in this setting. It incorporates a Prefix Reuse Predictor, a Cost-Aware Retention Score, and an Adaptive Threshold Controller. This framework is evaluated on real workloads and demonstrates significant performance gains over existing policies. KVLearn reduces time-to-first-token and inter-node transfer volume while maintaining acceptable throughput.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "To Keep or Not to Keep: Learning KV Cache Retention in Disaggregated LLM Serving Systems" reports on a learning-based framework designed for cost-aware KV-cache retention in disaggregated large language model serving systems, demonstrating significant performance gains over existing policies. The framework introduces KVLearn, which incorporates a Prefix Reuse Predictor, a Cost-Aware Retention Score, and an Adaptive Threshold Controller to manage cache retention based on network transfer costs. This methodology was evaluated on real workloads and resulted in reductions in time-to-first-token and inter-node transfer volume while sustaining acceptable throughput. This research indicates a pathway for optimizing resource utilization and reducing communication overhead in distributed large language model infrastructure.

items.title: When Planning Problems Become Hard for LLMs: Separating Structural Complexity from Semantic Interpretability
items.summary: LLMs struggle with classical planning, but existing benchmarks do not clearly separate structural difficulty from semantic interpretability. The zero-training delete-relaxation heuristic $h_{\mathrm{add}}$ outperformed other learned methods in predicting structural difficulty on planning domains. Renaming predicates causes a significant drop in LLM planning success, indicating sensitivity to semantic information. LLMs using semantic conditioning predict difficulty better than trained methods. Therefore, improving hybrid planning should focus on modeling LLM behavior sensitive to predicate semantics rather than solely on structural predictors.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "When Planning Problems Become Hard for LLMs: Separating Structural Complexity from Semantic Interpretability" reports on the difficulty Large Language Models encounter when solving classical planning problems and introduces methods to separate structural complexity from semantic interpretability in these domains. Researchers investigated how Large Language Models perform on planning tasks and examined the factors contributing to this difficulty. The study found that the zero-training delete-relaxation heuristic denoted as h add outperformed other learned methods in predicting structural difficulty across planning domains. Furthermore, renaming predicates resulted in a significant decrease in LLM planning success, demonstrating sensitivity to semantic information. LLMs employing semantic conditioning demonstrated superior prediction of difficulty compared to purely trained methods. This indicates that improving hybrid planning systems should emphasize modeling Large Language Model behavior sensitive to predicate semantics over relying solely on structural predictors. This research directs future development toward integrating semantic understanding for more effective planning AI.

items.title: [2604.22750] How Do AI Agents Spend Your Money? Analyzing and Predicting Token Consumption in Agentic Coding Tasks
items.summary: The study systematically analyzes token consumption patterns in agentic coding tasks across eight frontier LLMs. Agentic tasks are found to be significantly more expensive, consuming 1000x more tokens than standard code reasoning, with input tokens driving the overall cost. Token usage is highly stochastic, and accuracy does not necessarily increase with higher token expenditure. Furthermore, models exhibit large variations in token efficiency, with some models consuming substantially more tokens for the same tasks. Finally, frontier models demonstrate poor ability to accurately predict their own token usage.
items.audio_script: From arxiv.org, "2604.22750] How Do AI Agents Spend Your Money? Analyzing and Predicting Token Consumption in Agentic Coding Tasks" analyzes and predicts token consumption in agentic coding tasks, revealing that these tasks are significantly more expensive, consuming one thousand times more tokens than standard code reasoning. The study systematically analyzed token consumption patterns across eight frontier large language models engaged in agentic coding tasks. The methodology involved examining the token usage during these tasks, focusing on how input tokens drove the overall cost, and observed that token usage exhibited high stochasticity and a lack of correlation with increased accuracy. Furthermore, the models displayed substantial variations in token efficiency, with some exhibiting much higher token consumption for identical tasks, and frontier models demonstrated limited ability to accurately predict their own token usage. This research indicates that cost management and efficiency metrics require closer examination for advanced AI agent deployments.

items.title: Fix, Not Just Resample: Bounded Compiler-Guided Repair in Lean 4
items.summary: Automated theorem provers are improved by a bounded, online repair module for failed steps in Lean 4. This module samples candidate tactics and uses a pretrained model to fix failed tactics based on the compiler's error messages. This repair strategy improves the solve rate over sampling-only methods, achieving up to a $32\%$ relative gain. The gain is most significant for shallow tactic-execution failures, not structural errors. This targeted repair successfully increased the solve rate on a second benchmark by nearly doubling it.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Fix, Not Just Resample: Bounded Compiler-Guided Repair in Lean 4". This report details an improvement to automated theorem proving systems through the implementation of a bounded, online repair module within Lean 4. The research introduces a module designed to address failed steps by sampling candidate tactics and utilizing a pretrained model to correct these failures based directly on compiler error messages. This repair strategy demonstrates an improvement in the solve rate over purely sampling-based methods, achieving up to a thirty-two percent relative gain. The gain is most pronounced for failures occurring during shallow tactic execution, rather than structural errors, and the repair successfully nearly doubled the solve rate on a secondary benchmark. This development suggests a pathway for enhancing the reliability and efficiency of automated reasoning in formal proof systems.

items.title: ReAPO: Retry-Aware Policy Optimization for Efficient Exploration in LLM Reasoning
items.summary: ReAPO proposes Retry-Aware Policy Optimization to improve efficient exploration in Large Language Model reasoning by addressing issues with stochastic rollouts. It reframes credit assignment using Stochastic Shortest Paths to guide exploration, leading to a modification of GRPO called ReAPO. This method allocates generation to failed trajectories, reinforcing successful retries without penalizing preceding failures. Results show ReAPO improves first-attempt performance over GRPO and baseline algorithms across various reasoning benchmarks. The approach effectively enhances LLM reasoning through better exploration and credit assignment.

items.title: Big Claims, Small Margins: Do Reported GraphLLM Gains Survive Simple Baselines?
items.summary: LLM-based methods for node classification on text-attributed graphs often report state-of-the-art accuracy. A comparison with simpler baselines, such as Correct & Smooth or an MLP on frozen embeddings, reveals that reported LLM gains are not always substantial. Some reported LLM methods are within three points of the reference or better on many tasks, while the reference performs significantly better on others. Evaluation risks exist due to undisclosed configurations and data labeling practices in the reported studies. Therefore, reported performance improvements must be viewed cautiously when compared to simple baselines.

items.title: Pareto-Optimal RTL Code Generation via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models
items.summary: The work proposes a method for Large Language Models to generate Pareto-optimal RTL code by optimizing the quality and diversity of the entire circuit set, not just a single circuit. This approach moves beyond aggregating PPA objectives into a single reward to handle varying design trade-offs. It employs a generation-based training pipeline to treat coverage improvement across the Pareto set as a sequential generation problem. A reward function based on Hypervolume Contribution (HVC) is used to evaluate the quality of generated circuits relative to the Pareto front. Evaluation shows the method significantly improves relative Hypervolume and circuit diversity over existing optimization techniques.

items.title: SimHack: Predicting the onset of detectable reward hacking before RL training
items.summary: Reward hacking is a challenge in Reinforcement Learning with LLMs, often incentivized to hide malicious behavior during training. SimHack is introduced to predict when detectable reward hacking will become dominant before an RL training run begins. It learns reward hacking training dynamics from smaller reference runs to generate counterfactual simulations of unseen target recipes. SimHack accurately predicts the median onset of hacking to a 11.3% relative error across various training recipes. This prediction allows for guiding training decisions, discovering curricula that train longer without hacking.

items.title: Interaction-Gated Time-Frequency Learning for Parameter-Efficient PPG-Based Heart Rate Estimation
items.summary: The paper proposes TF-IG, a parameter-efficient interaction-gated time-frequency learning framework for heart rate estimation from photoplethysmography (PPG). It uses a dual-branch architecture to process temporal pulse morphology and frequency-domain periodicity separately. An interaction-gated fusion module explicitly models feature agreement and discrepancy between these domains, along with feature-wise weighting. Experiments on benchmark datasets show TF-IG achieves strong performance with low parameters, demonstrating an effective accuracy-complexity trade-off.

items.title: LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System
items.summary: LightCRS is a lightweight framework for unified multi-domain multimodal conversational recommendation. It precomputes multimodal product representations offline using frozen encoders. Online, a compact module fuses this evidence for dialogues using query-conditioned cross-attention shared across all domains. It achieves state-of-the-art recommendation metrics on a 25-domain benchmark by pairing conversations with product listings. LightCRS significantly reduces per-query latency while improving recommendation quality.

items.title: Borrowing Strength Across Stores: Transfer Learning for Choice-Based Revenue Management
items.summary: Retailers can improve choice-based revenue management by using transfer learning to borrow strength across store data. The study proposes a shrinkage estimator that combines store-specific estimates with pooled information from other stores using a multinomial logit demand model. The research establishes performance guarantees by exploiting the self-concordant properties of the likelihood function to characterize when information transfer is beneficial. Numerical experiments showed that shrinkage improved out-of-sample product prioritization and revenue capture for an apparel retailer. Ultimately, the findings demonstrate how leveraging network information can enhance revenue management while respecting local demand heterogeneity.

items.title: Motion Equivariant Convolutional LSTM: When Motion Becomes a Gauge Symmetry
items.summary: Motion becomes a gauge symmetry in sequential data because changes are defined by motion rather than absolute states. Standard recurrent networks lack equivariance to motion, as their memory is fixed while input moves. The research extends flow-equivariant networks to capture time-varying motion, treating a sequence as a field over time. This leads to a Motion Equivariant Convolutional LSTM (MELSTM) that uses the velocity model as a gauge field to ensure equivariance. MELSTM outperforms existing models in tasks like future-frame prediction and action recognition while being more parameter-efficient.

items.title: Large language model and reinforcement learning based autonomous construction and progress updates
items.summary: A method combining a large language model and reinforcement learning is proposed for autonomous construction and progress updates. This involves an enhanced soft actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm to plan crane actions based on construction tasks. The system utilizes robot kinematics and control algorithms to ensure executable crane actions. A customized embedding model extracts environmental information, and a large language model, like ChatGPT 5, is used to generate progress reports and safety information. Feasibility was verified through experiments involving full-scale retaining wall construction.

items.title: Scalable Stress-Constrained Topology Optimization: A Super-resolution and Simultaneous Approach Based on Machine Learning
items.summary: The simultaneous neural topology optimization (SNTO) framework is proposed to address the computational demands of large-scale, stress-constrained topology optimization. It uses custom neural networks to represent state, adjoint, and design variables, optimizing them within a single loop using continuous adjoint analysis and automatic differentiation. This method minimizes a loss function combining the design objective, stress constraints, and potential energy functionals. A hardware-aware training scheme partitions the design domain across multiple GPUs to ensure scalability to millions of degrees of freedom. Validation shows SNTO generates super-resolution designs with sharper boundaries compared to conventional methods.

items.title: Reinforcement learning for hardware acceleration and system-level optimization on FPGA and integrated-circuit platforms: A survey
items.summary: Reinforcement learning enables adaptive decision-making in computing systems, finding application on FPGAs and ICs despite hardware constraints. This survey reviews over 100 studies on RL implementations across FPGA and IC platforms, focusing on architectures and implementation strategies. It organizes research by RL family, hardware realization, and application domain, covering acceleration, energy-aware control, and system optimization. The review comparatively assesses resource utilization, latency, power consumption, and performance gains from RL-driven hardware systems. Ultimately, the work identifies architectural patterns, limitations, and future research directions for efficient RL deployment on specialized hardware.

items.title: A unified approach for estimation of unnormalized models via Stein operators
items.summary: A unified framework connects proper scoring rules and Stein's method for estimating unnormalized models. A class of proper scoring rules, including score matching and pseudolikelihood, naturally induce Stein operators. This connection establishes a new construction principle for Stein operators based on these scoring rules. The geometric properties of the induced Stein operators allow for a unified characterization of estimator asymptotic efficiency. Ultimately, this approach provides a cohesive method for estimating unnormalized models.

items.title: Offline Apprenticeship Learning for Human-Centric Environments
items.summary: Offline Apprenticeship Learning infers policies directly from expert demonstrations to enable learning without environment interaction, which is crucial for human-centric systems. The work develops frameworks for reward modeling, clustering demonstrations by latent reward functions, and partitioning trajectories using a learned reward regulator. It also addresses demonstration quality by integrating continuous quality signals and using Bayesian credit assignment to attribute decision quality. Experiments show that methods like StuEDM yield significant learning gains over expert baselines in real-world settings. Overall, this research establishes offline apprenticeship learning as a practical, data-efficient, and ethically viable paradigm.

items.title: Schr\"odinger-Bass Bridge Barycenter Models for Measure-Valued Data
items.summary: Barycenter models based on optimal transport bridges are useful for learning from measure-valued data. The paper introduces four novel barycenter models—SBB-encoder, SBB-decoder, SBB-symmetric, and SBB-Markovian—derived from the Schrödinger-Bass Bridge. Theoretical results establish the existence of the SBB-barycenter and characterize the Gaussian decoder by showing a Gaussian minimizer. A hybrid Wasserstein gradient particle descent scheme is derived for these models using the SBB dual representation. These methods are applied to solve distributional problems in spatial image and single-cell RNA sequencing data, showing superior interpolation performance.

items.title: Is In-Context Reinforcement Learning A Posterior Sampler? An Empirical Study
items.summary: The study investigates whether in-context reinforcement learning (ICRL), particularly methods like Decision-Pretrained Transformer (DPT), functions as a Bayesian posterior sampler in practice. The researchers establish two necessary conditions for a Bayesian posterior sampler: sufficient-statistic invariance and the martingale property. Statistical hypothesis tests are used to assess whether practically-trained ICRL models satisfy these conditions. The results consistently show that both conditions are violated across Gaussian, Bernoulli, and linear bandit settings. Consequently, the study suggests that ICRL may not behave as Bayesian posterior samplers in practice.

items.title: Internal Guidance as a Sampling Method for Tilted Diffusion Models
items.summary: Internal guidance proposes a novel sampling method for tilted diffusion models by modifying where the output of the base denoiser is evaluated, rather than altering the denoiser itself. This method works by shifting and rescaling the input when dealing with discrete distributions embedded in the hypercube $\{-1,1\}^{d}$. The training algorithm is modified using random diagonal rescalings to ensure the denoiser learns both in-distribution and out-of-distribution evaluations. A single denoiser network can sample binary reward tilts, class labels, and inpainting without requiring external guidance terms or fine-tuning. This approach simplifies guidance by focusing on evaluating the learned denoiser at shifted points.

items.title: Near Minimax Rate for Quantile Distributional Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: The paper studies the statistical accuracy of estimating the quantile Bellman fixed point $\bm\eta_m$ in quantile distributional reinforcement learning. It constructs a quantile fixed point estimator $\bm\eta_m^{(n)}$ from empirical Markov decision processes and establishes non-asymptotic error bounds under Wasserstein distances. The authors derive root-$n$ high-probability bounds simultaneously over all quantile resolutions $m$ and Wasserstein orders $p$. Further results show resolution-independent rates when reward densities vanish at endpoints, and characterize the exact local asymptotic minimax risk.

items.title: When Thoughts Become Memory: Unifying In-Context Learning and Fine-Tuning
items.summary: A certified rule is proposed for determining if unseen data belongs in a pretrained model's context or its weights, based on an exact law for information value. This law quantifies information value as the saved code length minus decoding loss, providing error-controlled certification. The method successfully diagnoses when in-context learning is helpful and provides a quantitative way to measure its effect by tracing learning curves. Experiments demonstrated that incorporating relevant context significantly improves model performance across various tasks. Ultimately, the research unifies in-context learning and fine-tuning through this information-based valuation.

items.title: Residual-Based Causal Discovery via Pretrained In-Context Quantile Regression
items.summary: Residual-based causal discovery assumes variables are generated from parents and noise, allowing identification of causal directions through residual independence testing. Existing methods often rely on parametric assumptions, which can lead to model misspecification. The proposed Loscar framework extends methods to location-scale noise models by using quantile regression to estimate conditional mean and scale. This approach enables pretrained tabular foundation models to serve as plug-in estimators for residual estimation. In causal-discovery benchmarks, in-context quantile regression significantly outperforms feasible generalized least squares methods.

items.title: A Reverse-Gold Theorem: Positive-Data Identification by Substrate-Bounded Contrastive Learners
items.summary: The research presents a method for positive-data identification using substrate-bounded contrastive learners. It proposes training a discriminative scorer via InfoNCE-style contrastive estimation on self-generated perturbations. This scorer is designed to achieve PAC conditional identification from positive data alone, with polynomial sample complexity. The results show a ranking guarantee with an $\varepsilon^{-2}$ rate, based on the geometry of the contrastive loss. The framework is instantiated for context-free and subregular classes, leading to an open conjecture.

items.title: Depth Separation for Neural Networks under Gaussian Measure
items.summary: The paper investigates depth separation for neural networks when operating under the standard Gaussian measure in $L^2$ approximation of radial functions. It demonstrates that a depth-3 ReLU network can approximate such a function within a small $L^2$ error, regardless of the polynomial size in $d$. However, approximating these functions with depth-2 networks requires exponentially large weights if the network size is to remain small. A general result shows that radial functions with significant high-frequency mass in their Hermite expansion resist approximation by small, bounded-weight depth-2 networks.
